context.requirement_text:
Source: GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016, BA checklist B2). Distinct roles do not stop ONE person who holds several roles, or the same role, from completing several steps of the SAME instance (meridian loan l1, l2, committee votes, D-ESC escalation, disbursement; the regulatory sign-off chain; vortex and swiftroute approvals). Precedent: self_approval_forbidden in lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex (approve_review). Implement exactly the REQ-459 design and slot the check into the order REQ-460 established in run_complete_task.
BINDING CONSTRAINTS (design-intent owner letflow-9a; not to be re-decided here): - identity is the USER ID, never the role; for an API-token request
  the identity is the token's user;
- enforced at COMPLETION as the authority and at CLAIM
  (Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3) as early feedback;
- NO role is exempt, TENANT_ADMIN included; - the completing user is compared against the MOST RECENT completion
  of each named node in the same instance, so rework loops work;
- BA decision 2026-10-07: a named node may lie on a PARALLEL branch
  (no path between the nodes); the check compares with the
  completions that exist at the time of the check, in any order, so
  whichever parallel node completes later must differ from the
  earlier completer; a named node that has not completed (path
  skipped, timer escalated past it) imposes no constraint;
- the attribute is OPTIONAL and OFF by default: definitions without it
  behave identically;
- the refusal is a clean 4xx with zero detail beyond 'separation of
  duties'.

BUILDS: 1. HUMAN_TASK node attribute `distinct_from: [node ids]`. 2. Completion check in Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task: if the actor
   is the user who most recently completed any listed node in this
   instance, refuse with the REQ-459 refusal body. Nothing is written
   except at most one audited refusal record without PII (exactly one
   when the audit store is healthy); the task stays open and
   claimable.
3. Claim check in Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3 with the same comparison
   and the same refusal body. Claim refusals write NO audit record.
4. Out of scope: org-chart or delegation models, a tenant-wide
   switch. DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07): assign_task/4 and
   reassign_task/4 do not check distinct_from; the completion check
   still refuses.

DESIGN FACTS (REQ-459 design; copy, do not re-decide): 5. ONE engine entry point, Letflow.Engine.SeparationOfDuties.check/5
   (repo, graph, task, actor_id, prefix), called by the
   `:completion_guards` step (design section 2.2 step 4b) that
   REQ-460 introduced, AFTER BOTH row locks (task, then instance
   projection) and BEFORE form re-evaluation and the merge, and
   before the rule C submitted check (4b before 4c). It returns :ok
   with no query when the node has no non-empty distinct_from or
   actor_id is not a binary; otherwise one query. On
   {:error, {:separation_of_duties, blocking_node_ids}} the step
   returns {:error, {:completion_refused, {:separation_of_duties, ids}}};
   the blocking node ids reach only the audit record, never the
   response. The claim path calls check_for_claim/3 (second public
   entry, loads the snapshot graph itself, delegates to check/5).
   check_for_claim/3 is TOTAL: any failure to obtain the graph or
   run the query (missing snapshot, failing build_graph/1, raise, DB
   error) is caught, logged with one Logger.warning naming only the
   task id and failure tag, and returns :ok (fails open; completion
   is the authority and re-checks under the locks). It runs only
   after the existing eligibility refusals, immediately before the
   write in the claim clauses and in the idempotent re-claim clause.
6. Rework read: one query per guarded completion or claim over
   `tasks` (status COMPLETED, instance_id, node_id IN named ids),
   DISTINCT ON (node_id) ordered node_id ASC, completed_at DESC,
   inserted_at DESC, id DESC, via the existing idx_task_instance
   index; NO migration and no new index. A named node with no
   completed row imposes no constraint; CANCELLED rows (escalated
   past) are never completions.
7. Refusal wire: HTTP 403, Content-Type application/problem+json,
   body EXACTLY {"detail":"separation of duties","status":403} (two
   members, constant bytes, no trace_id, no type/title) for EVERY
   cause (every node, user, instance) and on BOTH POST
   /tasks/:id/complete and POST /tasks/:id/claim, sent by
   Api.Response.separation_of_duties/1 (design section 4). The claim
   mapping deliberately diverges from claim's own 409 for
   eligibility refusals (D-2). Public engine error:
   {:error, :separation_of_duties}, detail-free.
8. Audit (design section 5): action task.completion_refused,
   after_state rule separation_of_duties with node_id and sorted
   blocking_node_ids; written by record_completion_refusal_audit/6
   (REQ-460 created it; this entry adds the {:separation_of_duties, _}
   half of completion_refusal()) after the failed transaction
   returns. At most one record per refused request, exactly one when
   the audit store is healthy; a failing audit store gives the same
   403 and one logged warning.
requirement_acceptance_criteria: two roles, one user: user U holds role-a and role-b, completes node N1 (role-a), then attempts node N2 (role-b, distinct_from [N1]): completion is refused with the REQ-459 4xx, the body is exactly the fixed separation-of-duties body, and the task is still open; a second user holding role-b completes N2 (real Postgres, engine and router tests)

the refusal is HTTP 403 and the body is exactly {"detail":"separation of duties","status":403}, byte-identical whichever node or user triggered it, and contains no node id, user id, user name or email (test compares bodies from two different triggers byte for byte and greps for the ids)

claim: U attempting POST /tasks/:id/claim on N2 is refused with the same 403 body and no audit record is written; a different eligible user claims successfully; a caller who is not eligible for the task still gets the existing claim refusal first (not the separation body); with the snapshot missing or build_graph/1 failing, check_for_claim/3 returns :ok, logs one warning and the eligible claim succeeds (fails open), and a definition without distinct_from gains no new claim failure
API-token case: a request authenticated with U's API token to complete N2 is refused, a token of a different user is accepted
TENANT_ADMIN is not exempt: a TENANT_ADMIN user who completed N1 is refused on N2 (requires REQ-447 PR2; the test fails if TENANT_ADMIN is special-cased)

parallel branches: nodes P1, P2 and P3 on parallel branches each name the other two in distinct_from; user U completes P1, then U attempting P2 is refused; three distinct users complete P1, P2 and P3 and all are accepted; the order of completion does not matter (U completing P2 first then attempting P1 is refused too)
a named node that never completed: N2 names N1, the path skipped N1, so U completes N2 with no refusal (test)
assign and reassign: assign_task and reassign_task to a user who completed a named node succeed (no check); the completion by that user is then refused

rework loop: U completes N1, a different user V completes N1 on a second pass, then U attempts N2: accepted because the most recent completion of N1 is V's; reversed order (V then U on the second pass) refuses U
default-off: a definition whose nodes carry no distinct_from lets the same user complete both steps, identical to today's behaviour (regression test on an existing shipped definition)

a refusal writes nothing except at most one audit record with no PII (exactly one when the audit store is healthy; rows before and after compared, including updated_at and event count; the record, action task.completion_refused, is searched for the user's email and name and contains neither); with audit_entries unavailable (DROP-TABLE regression) the refusal still returns the same 403, does not raise and one warning is logged; an armed escalation timer keeps its original fire_at after a refusal

a re-POST of an already-accepted completion by the same user is not refused by this rule: it receives the existing 409 'task is not pending' (the task is COMPLETED, so it ends at step 1 before the guards), the body is not the separation body and no task.completion_refused record is written (REQ-459 design section 10)
default-off query count: a completion of a node without distinct_from issues no additional query beyond today's
concurrency: two completions of parallel nodes P1 and P2 by the same user submitted concurrently: exactly one commits and the other is refused (the instance row lock serialises them)
SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict recorded (mandatory: authorization-adjacent change in lib/); it checks the refusal leaks nothing beyond 'separation of duties'
mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, scoped mix test over the engine and tasks router test files touched, and mix letflow.check_boundaries pass, real output quoted

STEP 02c - SECURITY GATE (SECURITY-REVIEWER), MANDATORY, hard gate. Review `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/` (ELIXIR-DEV commit 78e182a6) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-10 (state APPLIES / NOT-APPLICABLE for each, run the How-to-verify for each applicable), and against the design lib/letflow/design/req459-required-outputs-and-distinct-person.md rule A (sections 1.1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10). You are read-only on lib/: do not edit production code; report findings.

Explicitly check and give a verdict with file:line evidence for each:
1. The refusal leaks nothing beyond 'separation of duties': no node ids, user ids, names, emails in the HTTP body, headers, logs (the Logger.warning in check_for_claim/3 names only task id + failure tag), the public engine error ({:error, :separation_of_duties}), or the audit record (no PII; node ids allowed only in the audit after_state). Body bytes constant for every cause; both POST /tasks/:id/complete and POST /tasks/:id/claim.
2. Timing/side-channel differences between causes (which node, which user) and the claim-path difference between 'no such task' vs 'refused' (INV-5: not-found/forbidden indistinguishability; the separation check must run only AFTER the existing eligibility refusals so it cannot be used to probe other tenants' tasks).
3. Tenant isolation (INV-1/6): the read is scoped to the task's own instance (and prefix/tenant); no cross-tenant read; no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input (INV-7; inspect the fragment usage).
4. The claim fail-open decision (check_for_claim/3 total) is acceptable because completion re-checks under the locks; confirm completion cannot be bypassed in any path (grep every caller that completes a HUMAN_TASK: run_complete_task, any other completion entry such as API-token, bulk, scheduler/escalation, form submit endpoints, services) - any completion path that bypasses :completion_guards is a finding.
5. API-token identity = the token owner's user id on both handlers (conn.assigns.auth_context.user_id), no role exemption anywhere (TENANT_ADMIN, platform roles).
6. Row-lock ordering/deadlock: the check runs after BOTH locks (task, then instance projection) in the existing order; the claim path's read cannot deadlock with it; the claim `mode: :savepoint` choice is safe (no half-written state, no swallowed error that leaves a poisoned transaction).
7. DISTINCT ON read correct for rework (most recent COMPLETED per named node; CANCELLED never a completion; parallel semantics), via idx_task_instance, no migration.
8. Audit: written after the failed transaction returns, at most one record, a failing audit store gives the same refusal and one warning (INV-8: no unhandled crash), never inside the rolled-back transaction.
9. A re-POST of an already-accepted completion still ends at the existing 409 before the guards (design 10).
FAIL immediately on any applicable invariant failing; list BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR findings. Complete the handoff result with verdict, per-INV table, findings, next_action ('Route to REVIEWER (2d)' on PASS, 'Rework ELIXIR-DEV' on FAIL). Do not run mix test suites; you may run `mix compile` style read-only commands sparingly (RAM is tight).
RUN CONSTRAINTS (every agent in this run):
- Branch feat/REQ-463-distinct-from-Q-1026 (from origin/main 508163d0). Verify with `git branch --show-current` first; STOP and report if different. Do NOT push, open a PR, merge, touch the letflow-queue (lock 1026 is held by tvolodi-orch), touch branches feat/REQ-462-adopt-required-outputs-Q-1025 or test/authz-deny-log-deterministic-capture, or the untracked letflow-3.code-workspace. Stage files by explicit path only; never git add -A / git add . .
- Design: lib/letflow/design/req459-required-outputs-and-distinct-person.md governs rule A (distinct_from): sections 1.1, 2 (step 4b before 4c in the :completion_guards step), 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12.2 rule A plan, traceability A1-A11, 'Adjustments for REQ-460..466' for REQ-463. Where the requirement text and the design differ on a detail the DESIGN WINS; list every difference in result.design_vs_requirement_differences. REQ-464 (validator for distinct_from) is NOT this entry.
- RAM is VERY tight (0.4-2 GB free; the harness KILLS runs at critical memory). mix commands strictly sequential, ONE BEAM at a time; before each mix test check free RAM: powershell -NoProfile -c "[math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,2)". Scoped single test FILES only (never a directory or the full suite). `export MIX_TEST_PARTITION=3` ONLY for tests (unset for tooling tasks like compile/format/check_*); use a unique number (e.g. 15) for files that mutate shared state or run concurrency tests. If a run is killed, report it and do NOT loop.
- Real Postgres only. Never report 'should pass'; quote real Result: lines.
- docs/anti-patterns.md newest entry: a validator refusing at activate must be checked against EVERY test that activates hand-built definitions; grep the WHOLE test/ tree for the attribute, not only the changed area. REQ-461 check 2 applies: any test definition declaring required_outputs must declare a variable_schema for each key (register schema rows BEFORE activation); distinct_from needs no schema.
- Commit titles: feat|fix|test|docs|chore(REQ-463/Q-1026): ... [Q-1026 / GH #2341], ending with the trailer line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not commit your own handoff-file edits unless this handoff says so: ORCH commits after you return.
- Claim the handoff by setting top-level status to IN_PROGRESS only; at the end set status COMPLETED (or FAILED) and fill result (summary, verdict PASS/FAIL, issues, artifacts_out, evidence with quoted real output, next_action). Do not touch started_at/created_at. Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log.

explicit_checks.1_no_leak: PASS. Body: lib/letflow/api/response.ex @separation_of_duties_body constant (line ~61) sent by separation_of_duties/1 (~196-200), bypasses send_problem so no trace_id; same content-type mechanism as send_problem. Public engine error {:error, :separation_of_duties} (engine.ex interpret_complete_result clause, ids discarded as _ids). Logger.warning in separation_of_duties.ex warn_fail_open/2 names only task id + tag. Audit after_state: rule, instance_id, node_id, sorted blocking_node_ids, actor_id as the actor column (ids only, no name/email). Both handlers: routers/tasks.ex handle_complete_result({:error, :separation_of_duties}) and handle_claim_result(...) call the same function.
explicit_checks.2_timing_probe: PASS. Claim: SeparationOfDuties.check_for_claim runs inside apply_claim after fetch_and_lock_task and after the eligibility clauses (assignee_group_not_member / assignee_role_not_held / assigned_to_other_user return before it, tasks.ex ~448-500). Complete: guard runs after Tasks.authorize_completion in the router. The refusal path is identical for every node/user/instance (one query, one audit tx), no cause-dependent branch before the response.
explicit_checks.3_tenant_scope: PASS. separation_of_duties.ex blocking_nodes/6: Ecto query, repo.all([prefix: prefix] ++ query_opts), where instance_id == ^instance_id and node_id in ^named; actor cast with Ecto.UUID.cast; no interpolation. node ids come from the tenant's own snapshot graph.
explicit_checks.4_fail_open_and_bypass: PASS. The only HUMAN_TASK completion write is complete_task_row (engine.ex ~5326) reached only via run_complete_task <- complete_task/3; the only caller is routers/tasks.ex handle_complete (line 340). Other Task.complete_changeset uses (engine.ex 3099, 5859) set status :cancelled. No bulk/scheduler/service/form-submit path completes a task. :completion_guards runs after both locks and before any commit, so claim fail-open cannot bypass completion.
explicit_checks.5_identity: PASS. Both handlers use conn.assigns.auth_context.user_id (routers/tasks.ex 326 complete, 450 claim); no role comparison or exemption in separation_of_duties.ex (TENANT_ADMIN/platform roles not referenced). Token-vs-session is the same auth_context.
explicit_checks.6_locks: PASS. check runs inside the Multi after :task then :instance_projection locks (engine.ex ~2313-2322), plain SELECT, no new locks. Claim read is an unlocked SELECT on other rows while holding only the claimed task lock: no lock cycle possible. mode: :savepoint wraps the query so a DB error rolls back only the savepoint; the error is caught in check_for_claim and fails open; the claim transaction is not poisoned.
explicit_checks.7_distinct_on: PASS. Query: status == :completed, distinct node_id asc, order_by completed_at desc, inserted_at desc, id desc (Ecto prepends the distinct column); cancelled/pending never counted; named node with no completed row yields no tuple (no constraint); parallel semantics fall out of reading existing completions; idx_task_instance (migration 20260818110003) serves instance_id; no migration in diff.
explicit_checks.8_audit: PASS. record_completion_refusal_audit/6 is called from interpret_complete_result after Repo.transaction returned the failed Multi; own Repo.transaction, function-level rescue, log-and-swallow, always :ok; one call per refusal. Failing store: same 403 and one warning.
explicit_checks.9_repost_409: PASS. fetch_and_lock_task (engine.ex 2505-2514) returns {:task_not_pending, status} for non-pending rows at step 1, before :completion_guards; router maps it to 409 'task is not pending' (routers/tasks.ex 364).

NOTES: Informational: the 403 vs the 409 of eligibility refusals on claim lets an eligible caller tell 'separation of duties' from other claim refusals; that is the decided design (D-2) and reveals only the caller's own history.
